pages.title: Installing Shape
pages.description: Download and install Shape on Windows.
pages.body: Windows 10 or later (64 bit) Git (for clone and source control) Node.js (recommended for scripts and language tooling) You can open local projects without an account. Sign in is required for cloud AI. 1. Download the Windows installer from useshape.org/download. 2. Run the installer. If Windows SmartScreen warns that the app is unrecognized, choose More info , then Run anyway (common for new release hashes). 3. Open Shape from the Start menu. 1. File → Open Folder and pick a project. 2. Open the terminal ( View → Terminal or Ctrl+ ). If both work, you are set. Continue with Quick Start. Shape checks for updates automatically. Use Help → Check for Updates , or follow the titlebar prompt when one is available. In Settings → Account , switch the update channel to Pre release or turn off automatic checks. Shape will not start Restart Windows and try again. Re run the installer. Check that antivirus is not blocking Shape. Git or Node missing in the terminal Install Git for Windows and Node.js, then restart Shape. Quick Start Accounts

pages.title: Quick Start
pages.description: Open a project, learn the essential commands, and try AI chat.
pages.body: This guide gets you from a fresh install to productive editing in a few minutes. When Shape opens without a project, the center of the workbench shows quick actions: Action What it does Open Project Choose a folder on disk Open Terminal Open the bottom terminal panel Open AI Chat Open the chat panel Clone Repository Clone a Git URL into a folder you pick Reopen the welcome flow anytime from Help → Welcome . File → Open Folder , or use Ctrl+K Ctrl+O . Pick the folder that contains your code. The Explorer lists files; click one to open it in the editor. To clone instead: use Clone Repository on the welcome screen, paste a Git URL, and choose a parent folder. Action Shortcut Command palette Ctrl+Shift+P Quick open file Ctrl+P Find in project Ctrl+Shift+F Toggle terminal Ctrl+ Open settings Ctrl+, Toggle AI chat Ctrl+L If you forget a shortcut, search for the action in the command palette. Open Settings ( Ctrl+, ). Common first stops: Appearance — color theme (Dark, Graphite, One, Purple) Editor — font, format on save, tab size AI — model defaults and MCP servers via mcp.json Open the chat panel and send a question about the open project. Use @ mentions to attach files, folders, the codebase, or the current selection. Review proposed edits in the chat UI before applying them. See Chat overview and Chat modes. Installing Shape Accounts First project tutorial

pages.title: Accounts
pages.description: Shape account for AI, and GitHub sign-in for remotes.
pages.body: Shape has two sign in flows. They do different jobs and do not replace each other. Your Shape account unlocks cloud AI: chat, edits, indexing, and model selection. 1. Open the avatar menu in the titlebar. 2. Choose Sign in to Shape . 3. Finish in the browser, then return to the app. Local editing, Git, and the terminal work without a Shape account. Sign out from the same menu. Paid models use credits. The app may show remaining credits for convenience; allow/deny for each request is decided on the server. See Models and Pricing. GitHub sign in authenticates Git against GitHub remotes. It is separate from your Shape account. 1. Open the avatar menu. 2. Under GitHub, choose Sign in with GitHub . 3. Authorize Shape in the browser. Use it for fetch/push without repeated HTTPS prompts. Sign out only clears remote auth; local commits stay on disk. Shape account GitHub Purpose AI, models, credits Push/pull to GitHub Needed for local editing No No Needed for AI chat Yes No Needed for git push to GitHub No Recommended Chat Overview GitHub Sign In Models and Pricing

pages.title: Workbench Tour
pages.description: Learn the main regions of the Shape workbench and how they fit together.
pages.body: The workbench is Shape's main editing surface. Everything you do, from editing files to running Git and chatting with AI, happens inside this layout. Shape divides the window into five regions: Activity bar : narrow strip on the far left; switches sidebar views Primary sidebar : file tree, search, Git, outline, and more Editor : tabbed Monaco code area in the center Secondary sidebar : AI chat on the right Bottom panel : terminal and diagnostic views The titlebar holds: Menus : File, Edit, View, Go, Terminal, Window, Help Sidebar toggle : show or hide the primary sidebar Scripts dropdown : npm scripts for the open project Panel toggle : terminal and bottom views AI Chat toggle : right sidebar Settings and Reset Layout buttons Avatar menu : Shape account and GitHub sign in Drag the titlebar to move the window (on Windows, outside the menu buttons). Without a folder open, the editor area shows the welcome screen with Open Project, Clone Repository, Terminal, and AI Chat shortcuts. See Quick Start. With a folder open but no file selected, the center prompts you to pick a file from the Explorer or press Ctrl+P . Every major region can be hidden for focus: Region How to toggle Primary sidebar Titlebar sidebar button, or click the active activity bar icon again Bottom panel Titlebar panel button, View → Terminal , or Ctrl+ AI chat Titlebar chat button, or View → AI Chat All chrome Zen Mode with Ctrl+K Z Use Reset Layout in the titlebar to restore the default arrangement. Settings and Keyboard Shortcuts open as editor tabs instead of separate windows when launched from the activity bar or menu. Close them like any other tab with Ctrl+W . Activity Bar Titlebar and Panels Layout and Zen Mode Quick Start

pages.title: Activity Bar
pages.description: Switch between Explorer, Search, Git, and other sidebar views from the activity bar.
pages.body: The activity bar is the vertical strip on the far left of the workbench. Each icon opens a different view in the primary sidebar . Icon View Purpose File Explorer Browse and open project files Branch Source Control Stage, commit, and review changes Commit Git Graph Visual commit history List Outline Symbols in the active file Search Search Find and replace across the workspace Click an icon to switch views. Click the same icon again to collapse the sidebar entirely. When you have unsaved files, the Explorer icon shows a small badge with the count of dirty tabs. Save with Ctrl+S or File → Save All to clear it. Below the view icons, the activity bar has two fixed buttons: Button Action Terminal icon Opens the Command Palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P ) Gear icon Opens Settings These are shortcuts, not sidebar views. Settings opens in an editor tab. Every activity bar view is also available from View in the menu bar: View → Explorer ( Ctrl+Shift+E ) View → Search ( Ctrl+Shift+F ) View → Source Control ( Ctrl+Shift+G ) View → Git Graph View → Outline Use whichever path fits your workflow. Some features live elsewhere: AI Chat : titlebar toggle or View → AI Chat (right sidebar) Terminal : bottom panel, not the activity bar Problems / Output : bottom panel tabs Bookmarks : keyboard only ( Ctrl+Alt+B ); no activity bar entry File Explorer Workbench Tour Source Control Bookmarks

pages.title: Titlebar and Panels
pages.description: Use titlebar toggles, the scripts menu, and the bottom panel for terminal and diagnostics.
pages.body: The titlebar controls window level actions and layout. The bottom panel hosts the terminal and diagnostic output. App icon : branding (Windows) Sidebar toggle : show or hide the primary sidebar Menu bar : File, Edit, View, Go, Terminal, Window, Help On narrow windows, overflow menus collapse into a ⋯ menu so critical items stay reachable. When a file is open, the center shows the project path and filename. This region is draggable for window movement. Control Function Scripts Run npm scripts from package.json Panel Toggle the bottom panel (terminal, problems) AI Chat Toggle the right sidebar Settings Open Settings tab Reset Layout Restore default panel sizes Avatar Shape account and GitHub sign in The bottom panel stacks tabbed views: Tab Opens from Purpose Terminal View → Terminal , Ctrl+ , panel toggle Shell in project directory Problems View → Problems , Ctrl+Shift+M , command palette ESLint, TypeScript, and LSP diagnostics Output Command palette View: Show Output Tool and extension logs Tests Test runner integration Test results when available Click a tab to switch views. Drag the top edge of the panel to resize it. When a package.json with a scripts section is in the open project, the Scripts button appears in the titlebar. 1. Click Scripts . 2. Choose a script (for example dev , build , test ). 3. Shape runs it in the integrated terminal and opens the panel if needed. See NPM Scripts for details. Primary sidebar (left): persistent project tools like files, Git, and search Secondary sidebar (right): AI chat Bottom panel : transient command output like terminal, problems, and tests Toggling the panel does not close your terminal session. It hides the panel until you show it again. If panels feel misplaced or too small, click Reset Layout (desktop windows icon) in the titlebar. This restores: Primary sidebar open Bottom panel open AI chat closed It does not close open files or change your project. Integrated Terminal Problems, Output, and Tests NPM Scripts Workbench Tour

pages.title: Command Palette
pages.description: Run workbench and editor commands, search files, jump to symbols, and browse chat history.
pages.body: The command palette is Shape's universal action search. Open it with Ctrl+Shift+P or from View → Command Palette… . Type to filter commands. Press Enter to run the selected action, or Escape to close. In default mode, the palette lists: Workbench commands : panels, settings, chat history, zen mode Editor commands from the active file: format, rename, fold, comment Commands show keyboard shortcuts on the right when assigned. Fuzzy matching works on both label and shortcut fragments. You can also open the palette from the activity bar bottom button (terminal icon). Go to File opens a dedicated files mode, not the full command list. 1. Press Ctrl+P (or Go → Go to File… ). 2. Type part of a filename. 3. Press Enter to open the match. This mode is optimized for speed. In Shape, Ctrl+Shift+P and Ctrl+P are separate shortcuts. Jump to a specific line (and optionally column): 1. Press Ctrl+G ( Go → Go to Line/Column… ). 2. Type a line number, or line:column (for example 42:8 ). 3. Press Enter . The editor scrolls and places the cursor at that position. Find functions, classes, and variables across the project: 1. Press Ctrl+T or run Go to Symbol in Workspace… from the palette. 2. Type a symbol name. 3. Select a result to open the defining file at that location. Indexing quality depends on language support and LSP configuration. See IntelliSense. Browse past AI conversations: 1. Open the command palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P ). 2. Run Chat: Show History . 3. Select a conversation to reopen it in the AI sidebar. Useful when you need to continue an earlier thread without scrolling the chat panel. Change syntax highlighting for the active file: 1. Open the palette and run Change Language Mode… . 2. Pick a language from the filtered list (TypeScript, Markdown, CSS, etc.). Shape remembers the association for that file path. Language mode affects highlighting, snippets, and LSP behavior. Quick Fix ( Ctrl+. ) is an editor action, not the palette, but you can find it by typing quick fix in the palette. Palette only commands (no default shortcut) include View: Show Problems , View: Show Output , Editor: Toggle Minimap , and Chat: Show History . When the palette is open, arrow keys navigate. Typing immediately filters. Keyboard Shortcuts Quick Start Workspace Search Chat Overview

pages.title: Layout and Zen Mode
pages.description: Resize sidebars, reset the layout, and hide all chrome with Zen Mode.
pages.body: Shape's layout is flexible. Collapse sidebars, resize the bottom panel, and enter Zen Mode for distraction free editing. Open : click any activity bar icon, or use View → Explorer (etc.) Close : click the active activity bar icon again, or use the titlebar sidebar toggle Resize : drag the divider between sidebar and editor The sidebar remembers which view was active (Explorer, Search, Git, etc.). Open : titlebar AI Chat button or View → AI Chat Close : click the toggle again Resize : drag the divider between editor and chat Toggle : titlebar panel button, View → Terminal , or Ctrl+ Resize : drag the top edge of the panel upward or downward The terminal keeps running when the panel is hidden. Click Reset Layout in the titlebar (desktop windows icon) to restore defaults: Region Default state Primary sidebar Open Bottom panel Open Secondary sidebar (AI) Closed Reset does not affect open files, Zen Mode preference, or sidebar view selection. Zen Mode hides the activity bar, both sidebars, and the bottom panel, leaving only the editor and titlebar menus. View → Zen Mode Command palette: View: Toggle Zen Mode Ctrl+K Z (chord: press Ctrl+K , release, then Z ) Press the same shortcut again to exit. Your panel open/closed state is restored. Writing or reviewing a long file without sidebar noise Presenting code in a meeting Pairing where chat and Git panels are not needed temporarily Zen Mode does not change font size or word wrap. Adjust those in Editor Settings. For side by side editing, use the tab bar split actions (see Tabs and Splits). Splits work inside Zen Mode. Only chrome is hidden, not multi group editing. Workbench Tour Titlebar and Panels Tabs and Splits Keyboard Shortcuts

pages.title: Editing Files
pages.description: Open, edit, save, and format files in the Shape editor.
pages.body: The Shape editor is built on Monaco, the same engine that powers VS Code. It provides syntax highlighting, multi cursor editing, and language aware features for web projects. Action Menu Shortcut Open file File → Open File Ctrl+O Open folder File → Open Folder Ctrl+K Ctrl+O New file File → New Text File Ctrl+N Quick open Go → Go to File… Ctrl+P New files from File → New Text File appear in the Explorer when saved. New Scratch File creates a temporary buffer without a path until you save. Action Shortcut Save Ctrl+S Save As Ctrl+Shift+S Save All Ctrl+K S Close tab Ctrl+W Close all tabs Ctrl+K E Dirty tabs show a dot indicator. The Explorer activity bar badge counts unsaved files. Standard text operations work as expected: Undo / Redo : Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Cut / Copy / Paste : Ctrl+X / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V Select All : Ctrl+A Hold Alt and click to add cursors. Use Ctrl+Alt+↑ and Ctrl+Alt+↓ to add cursors on adjacent lines. Ctrl+Shift+L selects all occurrences of the current selection. Action Shortcut Move line up/down Alt+↑ / Alt+↓ Duplicate line down Shift+Alt+↓ Toggle line comment Ctrl+/ Toggle block comment Shift+Alt+A Indent / outdent Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ Format the whole file with Edit → Format Document or Alt+Shift+F . Shape uses Prettier when configured for the project. Format only the selection via the command palette: Format Selection ( Ctrl+K Ctrl+F ). Go to Line : Ctrl+G Go to Definition : F12 (requires language support) Go to Bracket : Ctrl+Shift+\\ Back / Forward : Alt+Left / Alt+Right through cursor history Toggle wrap from View → Word Wrap or the command palette ( Editor: Toggle Word Wrap , Alt+Z ). Enable auto save in Settings → Editor . Choose delay or save on focus change. See Editor Settings. Languages and tooling Tabs and Splits IntelliSense Command Palette Editor Settings

pages.title: Tabs and Splits
pages.description: Manage editor tabs, split groups, and preview modes for open files.
pages.body: Shape opens every file in a tab at the top of the editor. Tabs support preview modes, split groups, and quick navigation across your working set. Action Shortcut Close active tab Ctrl+W Close all tabs Ctrl+K E Reopen closed tab Command palette: Reopen Closed Editor Dirty tabs show a dot on the label. Save with Ctrl+S before closing if you want to keep changes. Click a tab to switch files. Middle click a tab (or use the close icon) to close it. Split the editor to view two files side by side: 1. Click the Split Editor Right button on the tab bar, or use the tab context menu. 2. The active file moves to the right group. The left group keeps its previous file. 3. Click Close Split to return to a single group. Each split group has its own tab strip and active file. Drag tabs between groups when both are visible. Splits work in Zen Mode. Only sidebars are hidden, not multi group editing. Some file types support alternate views from the tab bar toggle: File type Modes Markdown Source, split, and rendered preview Images Raw path and inline preview Fonts Source and live preview For Markdown, cycle through Source , Split View , and Preview with the toggle on the tab. Split view shows the editor and preview at the same time. Git changes open as special diff tabs labeled Working Tree or Index . These are read only comparison views. See Diff and Merge. Tabs reflect open order. The most recently used file becomes active when you click its tab or open it from the Explorer. Use Ctrl+P to jump between files without clicking tabs. Editing Files Markdown Preview Diff and Merge Layout and Zen Mode

pages.title: Markdown Preview
pages.description: Render Markdown files with live preview and split view in the editor.
pages.body: Shape renders Markdown files with a built in preview powered by the same tab you use for source editing. Switch between source, split, and preview without leaving the workbench. Open any .md or .mdx file from the Explorer or with Ctrl+P . Syntax highlighting applies in source mode. Use the mode toggle on the tab bar to cycle views: Mode What you see Source Raw Markdown in the Monaco editor Split Editor on one side, rendered preview on the other Preview Full width rendered output Split view is useful when editing documentation and checking headings, links, and code blocks at the same time. The preview renders standard Markdown elements: Headings, paragraphs, and lists Links and images (relative paths resolve from the file location) Fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting Blockquotes and inline formatting Complex MDX components used in Shape's own docs site may not render identically in the IDE preview. The preview targets common Markdown, not full MDX execution. In split mode, edit on the left and confirm layout on the right. Save with Ctrl+S to persist changes. The preview updates when the file content changes. Use Ctrl+Shift+P and run Change Language Mode… if a file is not detected as Markdown. For long docs, Zen Mode plus split preview gives a focused writing surface. Pair preview with Bookmarks to jump between sections you are revising. Tabs and Splits Editing Files Design Tools

pages.title: Diff and Merge
pages.description: Review Git changes, inline diffs, and AI-proposed edits in comparison views.
pages.body: Shape shows file differences in dedicated diff tabs so you can review changes before committing or accepting AI edits. From Source Control , click a changed file to open a diff tab. Tabs are labeled with the filename and context: Label Meaning Working Tree Unstaged changes vs the index Index Staged changes vs the last commit The diff view uses Monaco's inline comparison with added and removed highlighting. Read the changes, then stage or discard from the Source Control sidebar. In the Git Graph, right click a commit and choose Compare with Working Tree or View Changes to inspect historical diffs. When AI chat edits files in Code mode, each change appears as a review card after it is written to disk. 1. Click the file (or Preview ) to open a diff in the editor. 2. Compare the latest step against the previous version. 3. Keep leaves the file as written. Undo restores the baseline from before the unresolved edit chain. See Reviewing Edits for the full Keep/Undo workflow. If a git pull or merge produces conflicts, Shape surfaces conflict markers in the affected files. Open the file in the editor and look for standard conflict sections: Resolve conflicts manually in the editor, then stage the file and commit. Shape does not yet provide a dedicated three way merge UI. Use the diff tabs and editor for manual resolution. Close diff tabs with Ctrl+W when review is done. Unstaged and staged diffs open as separate tabs so you can compare both states. Enable Git: Blame in settings to see line attribution while reviewing changes. Source Control Reviewing Edits Tabs and Splits Git Graph

pages.title: Design Tools
pages.description: Tailwind controls, color picker, and design diagnostics in the editor.
pages.body: Shape includes design aware tooling for web UI work. Completions, inline controls, and diagnostics help you edit Tailwind classes and CSS variables without leaving the editor. When your cursor is inside a className string, Shape can show inline controls for common utilities: Flex / Grid : direction, wrap, justify content, align items. Click the swatch next to a flex or grid token Gap : column and row gap. Click a gap token Padding : per side padding. Click a p / px / pl token Color picker : Tailwind palette and project CSS variables Controls appear as a floating panel near the attribute. Click a value to apply it directly to the source. Toggle controls in Settings → Design Tools → Tailwind Controls . Shape suggests Tailwind semantic tokens, CSS design variables, and in project class patterns while you type inside className attributes and style blocks. Enable or disable this in Settings → Design Tools → Design Autocomplete . Opening a parent folder (for example a repo that contains shape/ and website/ as separate git roots) discovers each nested repository for Source Control and explorer decorations. Accessibility checks run on color contrast and related design issues in supported files (JSX, TSX, CSS). Violations appear as squiggles in the editor and in the Problems panel. Configure severity in Settings → Design Tools → Design Diagnostics . Choose AA or AAA contrast level. The color picker reads from: Tailwind's default palette CSS variables defined in project files like design tokens.css Picking a color inserts the matching class or variable reference at the cursor. The chat panel includes a Design mode tuned for UI and styling changes. It follows existing project patterns before introducing new styles. See Chat Modes. IntelliSense Lint and LSP AI Settings Chat Modes

pages.title: IntelliSense
pages.description: Completions, hovers, go-to-definition, and diagnostics from language servers.
pages.body: IntelliSense is Shape's language aware assistance in the Monaco editor. Completions, hovers, diagnostics, and navigation come from built in language servers and editor services. Start typing to see suggestions. Press Tab or Enter to accept. Shape enables language servers for common web stacks: Language Features TypeScript / JavaScript Types, imports, refactor hints CSS / HTML Selectors, tags, attributes JSON Schema aware keys and values Tailwind CSS Class name completions in className Toggle individual servers in Settings → Languages & LSP . When a diagnostic offers a fix, a lightbulb appears in the gutter. Press Ctrl+. to open Quick Fix and choose an action. Common fixes include adding imports, fixing ESLint violations, and applying TypeScript corrections. Action Shortcut Go to Definition F12 Peek Definition Alt+F12 Find All References Shift+F12 Go to Symbol in Workspace Ctrl+T Go to Next Problem F8 Go to Previous Problem Shift+F8 Go to Symbol in Editor is available from the command palette for symbols in the current file. Hover over a symbol to see type information, documentation, and color previews for CSS values. Hold Ctrl and hover a symbol to peek its definition inline. Errors and warnings appear as squiggles in the editor and aggregate in the Problems panel ( Ctrl+Shift+M ). Sources include: TypeScript compiler ESLint (when enabled) Design diagnostics for contrast issues Tailwind CSS language service Fix issues in the editor or open Problems to jump between files. Place the cursor on a symbol and press F2 to rename it across the project. Preview changes before confirming. Lint and LSP Design Tools Problems, Output, and Tests Command Palette

pages.title: File Explorer
pages.description: Browse, create, rename, and manage files in the project tree.
pages.body: The Explorer is the default primary sidebar view. It shows the folder you opened with File → Open Folder as a collapsible tree. Click the file icon on the activity bar View → Explorer or Ctrl+Shift+E After opening a project, the Explorer loads automatically Click a file to open it in a new editor tab. Click folders to expand or collapse them. Use Ctrl+P for faster navigation when you know the filename. Modified, added, and deleted files show color cues in the tree. These match the status reported in Source Control. Refresh happens when you save, stage, or run Git commands. Right click a folder or empty area for context actions: New File New Folder Rename Delete Copy / Cut / Paste You can also use File → New Text File ( Ctrl+N ) to create a file at the project root. With a file open in the editor, run Reveal in Explorer from the command palette to scroll the tree to that file's location. The Explorer header includes buttons to collapse all folders and refresh the tree. Refresh is useful after external tools add or remove files outside Shape. Unsaved open files show a badge on the Explorer activity bar icon with the count of dirty tabs. Save all with Ctrl+K S . Workspace Search Tabs and Splits Source Control Activity Bar

pages.title: Workspace Search
pages.description: Find and replace text across all files in the open project.
pages.body: The Search sidebar finds text across your entire workspace. Use it for refactors, auditing string usage, and locating config keys. Click the search icon on the activity bar View → Search or Ctrl+Shift+F Edit → Find in Files from the menu 1. Type your search query in the search box. 2. Results appear grouped by file with line previews. 3. Click a result to open the file at that line. Search respects file exclude patterns from Settings → Files . Hidden folders like node modules are skipped by default. Switch to replace mode with Ctrl+H or the toggle in the search sidebar. 1. Enter find and replace strings. 2. Review matches in the results list. 3. Replace one match at a time, or replace all in a file or across the workspace. Confirm bulk replacements carefully. Shape modifies files on disk when you apply a replace. Use the buttons below the search field to toggle: Match case Match whole word Use regular expression Regex mode supports capture groups in replace strings. Feature Shortcut Scope Go to File Ctrl+P Filenames only Find in Files Ctrl+Shift+F File contents Workspace Symbols Ctrl+T Functions, classes, variables Use Ctrl+P when you know the file name. Use search when you need to find text inside files. Command Palette File Explorer IntelliSense Keyboard Shortcuts

pages.title: Outline
pages.description: Jump to functions, classes, and symbols in the active editor file.
pages.body: The Outline sidebar lists symbols defined in the file you are editing. Use it to navigate long files without scrolling. Click the list icon on the activity bar View → Outline from the menu bar The outline updates when you switch tabs. It reflects the active editor file only, not the whole workspace. Symbols depend on the file language and LSP support: Language Typical symbols TypeScript / JavaScript Functions, classes, interfaces, variables CSS Rules and selectors HTML Elements and sections Markdown Headings If symbols are missing, check that the correct language mode is set and the relevant LSP is enabled in Lint and LSP. Click any entry to move the cursor to that symbol in the editor. The editor scrolls and focuses the definition. For project wide symbol search, use Ctrl+T ( Go to Symbol in Workspace ). The titlebar breadcrumbs show the file path. The outline shows structure inside the file. Use both together when working in large modules. IntelliSense Command Palette Activity Bar Editing Files

pages.title: Bookmarks
pages.description: Mark lines in files and jump between bookmarks across the workspace.
pages.body: Bookmarks let you save positions in code and return to them later. Bookmarks persist in local storage across sessions. 1. Place the cursor on the line you want to mark. 2. Press Ctrl+Alt+B . A bookmark icon appears in the editor gutter. Press Ctrl+Alt+B again on the same line to remove it. Action Shortcut Next bookmark Ctrl+F2 Previous bookmark Shift+F2 Navigation wraps around. If the next bookmark is in another file, Shape opens that file and moves the cursor. Open the command palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P ) and search for Bookmarks to see the bookmark list panel. Each entry shows the file path, line number, and a short label. Click an entry to jump to that location. Remove bookmarks from the list when you no longer need them. By default, bookmarks use the label Line N . When you toggle a bookmark on a word, Shape may use that word as the label. Bookmarks are per workspace path and stored locally. They are not synced to Git or your Shape account. Clearing browser or app storage removes them. Bookmark failing tests, TODO comments, or sections you revisit during a refactor. Bookmarks have no activity bar icon. Use keyboard shortcuts or the command palette. Combine with Outline for within file structure and bookmarks for cross file anchors. Editing Files Activity Bar Keyboard Shortcuts Command Palette

pages.title: Source Control
pages.description: Stage changes, write commits, and sync with remotes from the Git sidebar.
pages.body: The Source Control sidebar is Shape's built in Git panel. Stage files, write commits, and push or pull without leaving the IDE. Click the branch icon on the activity bar View → Source Control or Ctrl+Shift+G Click the branch indicator in the status bar The Changes section lists modified, added, and deleted files. Click a file to open a diff tab. Action How Stage one file Click the + icon next to the file Unstage Click the − icon on a staged file Stage all Click + on the Changes header Discard Right click and choose discard (confirm when prompted) 1. Stage the files you want included. 2. Enter a commit message in the text box at the top. 3. Optionally add a longer description in the second field. 4. Click Commit or press Ctrl+Enter . If Confirm Before Commit is enabled in Git settings, Shape asks you to confirm first. Click the sparkle icon next to the commit message field to generate a suggested title and description from your staged diff. The toolbar includes: Button Action Pull Fetch and merge from the tracked remote branch Push Upload local commits Sync Pull then push in one step Refresh Reload Git status Sign in with GitHub to avoid credential prompts on push. If the open folder is not a Git repository, Source Control shows an Initialize Repository action. Click it to run git init in the project root. The bottom status bar shows the current branch and ahead/behind counts. Click it to open Source Control. Branches and Remotes Diff and Merge Git Graph Git Settings

pages.title: Branches and Remotes
pages.description: Switch branches, manage remotes, and keep your local repo in sync.
pages.body: Shape exposes common branch and remote operations from the Source Control sidebar and branch picker. You rarely need a separate terminal for day to day Git workflow. The branch name appears at the top of Source Control and in the status bar. Click it to open the branch picker . 1. Click the current branch name in Source Control. 2. Select a local branch from the list to check it out. 3. Shape runs git checkout and refreshes the file tree. Uncommitted changes may block checkout if they conflict. Commit or stash changes first. From the branch picker: 1. Choose Create new branch… 2. Enter a name (for example feature/auth ). 3. Shape creates the branch from your current HEAD and checks it out. You can also create a branch from the command palette or integrated terminal if you prefer the CLI. Manage remotes from the Source Control toolbar or remote dialog: Action Description Add remote Link a name (usually origin ) to a URL Edit remote Change the URL for an existing remote Remove remote Delete the remote reference (not the server repo) Paste an HTTPS or SSH URL when adding a remote. For GitHub HTTPS remotes, sign in with GitHub to simplify authentication. Pull downloads and merges remote changes into your current branch. Push uploads local commits the remote does not have yet. Sync runs pull then push. Enable Auto Fetch in Git Settings to refresh remote state on an interval. After fetch, the status bar and branch picker may show counts like ↑2 ↓1 meaning you are two commits ahead and one behind the tracked remote branch. Push and pull to reconcile. Source Control GitHub Sign In Git Graph Clone and Commit Tutorial

pages.title: Git Graph
pages.description: Explore commit history visually and inspect changes from the graph view.
pages.body: The Git Graph sidebar shows your repository's commit history as a lane diagram. Inspect past work, compare commits, and open file diffs from one view. Click the commit icon on the activity bar View → Git Graph from the menu bar The graph loads commits for the open Git repository. Large histories virtualize for performance as you scroll. Each row is a commit. Columns show: Lane lines : branch and merge topology Message : commit subject (click @mentions to open GitHub profiles) Author and relative time Expand a commit row to see files changed in that commit. Right click a commit for context actions: Checkout (detached HEAD or branch tip) Compare with Working Tree View file changes (opens diff tabs) Copy commit hash Use compare actions to understand what changed between a past commit and your current working tree. Use the search field at the top to filter commits by message or author. Clear the filter to show the full history again. Click the refresh button after external Git operations (terminal commands, pulls from another tool) to reload the graph. Source Control Diff and Merge Branches and Remotes Activity Bar

pages.title: GitHub Sign In
pages.description: Authenticate Git operations against GitHub remotes from the avatar menu.
pages.body: GitHub sign in lets Shape push and pull to GitHub without repeated password prompts. It is separate from your Shape account used for AI features. Sign in when you: Push commits to a GitHub HTTPS remote Pull from a private GitHub repository Want your GitHub username shown in the avatar menu Local Git operations (commit, branch, log) work without signing in. 1. Click the avatar in the titlebar. 2. Under GitHub , choose Sign in with GitHub . 3. Complete authorization in your browser. 4. Return to Shape. The menu shows @your username (GitHub) when connected. Shape stores credentials through Git's credential helper on Windows. Open the avatar menu → GitHub → Sign out . Your local repository data is unchanged. Only remote authentication is cleared. GitHub sign in requires Git tooling on your system: Git for Windows , or GitHub CLI If neither is installed, the avatar menu shows a note to install one. See Install for setup links. Confirm you approved the Shape OAuth application. Check your network and try again from the avatar menu. Verify the remote URL points to GitHub ( github.com ). Sign out and sign in again from the avatar menu. For SSH remotes, configure SSH keys outside Shape. GitHub sign in applies to HTTPS. Sign out, then sign in with the correct GitHub account. Credential helpers may cache the previous user until you clear them. Accounts Source Control Branches and Remotes Clone and Commit Tutorial

pages.title: Chat Overview
pages.description: Ask questions and edit code from the AI chat panel.
pages.body: AI Chat lives in the right sidebar. Ask about the project, get explanations, and request edits with review before anything is applied. Titlebar AI Chat toggle View → AI Chat Ctrl+L Drag the divider to resize. Use the same control to close the panel. Cloud AI needs a Shape account. Local editing does not. 1. Type in the input at the bottom of the panel. 2. Pick a mode (start with Ask for read only questions). 3. Choose a model, or leave Auto . 4. Press Enter to send ( Shift+Enter for a new line). Shape attaches workspace context when it helps: open files, project layout, and diagnostics. Use @ mentions for a file, folder, the codebase, or the current editor selection. Use the attachment control to add images or files (screenshots, design references, a specific file). Past chats are saved per project. Run Chat: Show History from the command palette to reopen one. Click Stop while a reply is streaming to cancel. Partial output stays in the thread. In Code and related modes, the assistant may propose shell commands. Each one shows Run or Reject before it executes. Chat Modes Reviewing Edits Models and Pricing AI Settings

pages.title: Chat Modes
pages.description: Choose Ask, Code, Plan, Design, or Review mode for each conversation.
pages.body: Each chat message runs in a mode that controls what the assistant can do. Pick the mode from the dropdown next to the input box before you send. Mode Behavior Best for Ask Read only. No file edits or terminal commands. Learning the codebase, explaining errors Code Can read, edit, and run commands. Proposes changes for review. Implementing features and fixes Plan Research only. Writes a markdown plan to .shape/plans/ . Designing an approach before coding Design UI and styling focused. Follows existing design patterns. Layout, Tailwind, and component polish Review Systematic investigation of bugs, failures, and security issues, with an optional adversarial self check. Tracking down runtime/build errors, auditing auth, input handling, and dependencies Safe default for exploration. The assistant reads your project and answers questions but cannot modify files or run the terminal. Use Ask when onboarding to a new repo. The default for implementation work. The assistant can: Read and search files Propose and apply edits shown as review cards (Keep / Undo) Run terminal commands (with your approval) Call finish when the task is done Switch to Code when you are ready to apply changes. See Reviewing Edits. Plan mode researches the codebase and saves an implementation plan as markdown under .shape/plans/ . Plans include a Todos checklist. It does not edit project source files. When the plan is ready, review the file and click Build this plan (or switch to Code and ask to implement). During build, the assistant maintains a live todo checklist in chat via update todos . Design mode prioritizes existing UI conventions in your project. It is tuned for Tailwind classes, component structure, and visual consistency. Mention @design in chat when you want the assistant to focus on UI work. Pair with Design Tools in the editor. Review mode combines systematic debugging with security minded review: it reads errors, logs, and relevant code before suggesting fixes, and watches for vulnerability patterns in auth flows, user input, and unsafe APIs. Enable the adversarial self check in AI settings to have a second pass challenge the first response before it's shown. Older Debug and Security selections are automatically migrated to Review — the two were folded into one mode. Change the mode between messages in the same thread. Earlier context carries over, but tool permissions follow the active mode for each new message. Chat Overview Reviewing Edits Refactor with AI Tutorial AI Settings

pages.title: Reviewing Edits
pages.description: Keep or undo AI file changes after the agent writes them to disk.
pages.body: In Code mode (and other editing modes), the assistant can change files on disk as it works. Each change shows up for review so you can Keep it or Undo it. 1. The agent writes the updated file to disk. 2. Chat shows an edit card with +/ line counts for that step. 3. Open the file (or use Preview ) to review the diff in the editor. 4. Keep dismisses the review and leaves the file as written. 5. Undo restores the file to how it was before this unresolved edit chain. If the agent edits the same file again before you Keep or Undo, the review updates to the latest step. Undo restores the baseline from before the first unresolved edit on that file. Each file change in the thread shows: The affected file path Added and removed line counts for that edit step Actions to open or review the change When files still need a Keep or Undo decision, a summary appears above the chat input. Use Keep All or Undo All , or handle files one at a time. By default, edits still appear for review after they are written. Enable Auto Apply Edits in AI Settings to auto Keep proposals as they arrive. Use this only when you trust the workflow. Separate from file edits, terminal commands show their own approval card. Click Run to execute in the integrated terminal or Reject to skip. The assistant cannot run shell commands without your approval. Kept and undone edits are tracked for the conversation. Reloading the project preserves which proposals you already resolved. If the agent edits a file again after you Keep it, a new review opens for that later change. Chat Modes Diff and Merge AI Settings Chat Overview

pages.title: AI Settings
pages.description: Configure models, context limits, auto-apply, custom rules, and MCP servers.
pages.body: AI behavior is controlled from Settings → AI in the settings editor tab. Open settings from the activity bar gear icon or File → Preferences → Settings . Setting Purpose Enabled models Toggle which models appear in the chat picker Default model Pre selected model for new threads Disable models you never use to simplify the dropdown. Max context lines limits how much surrounding code Shape sends with each message. Higher values give the assistant more file context but use more credits. Presets range from focused snippets to larger windows. When Auto Apply Edits is off (default), every file change requires explicit Accept in the chat panel. Turn it on only if you want proposals applied without confirmation. See Reviewing Edits. Two text fields shape assistant behavior: Custom system prompt : high level personality and priorities Custom rules : project specific conventions (naming, patterns, files to avoid) These append to the built in mode instructions for every message in the workspace. The indexing section shows progress for semantic codebase search. Re index after large refactors so AI search stays accurate. Index data is scoped to the open project. Model Context Protocol servers extend the assistant with external tools. Configure servers in the MCP section or open the MCP config file directly from settings. Each server entry includes: Name and launch command Arguments and environment variables Enabled toggle Restart or reconnect after changing MCP configuration. Models and Pricing Chat Overview Settings Overview Reviewing Edits

pages.title: Integrated Terminal
pages.description: Run shell commands in the project directory from the bottom panel.
pages.body: Shape embeds a full terminal in the bottom panel. It opens in your project root so install commands, dev servers, and Git CLI usage stay in context. Action Shortcut Toggle panel Ctrl+ New terminal tab Ctrl+Shift+ Menu View → Terminal or Terminal → New Terminal Titlebar Click the panel toggle The panel remembers open tabs when you hide it. The default shell follows Settings → Terminal → Default Shell : Auto (system default on Windows) PowerShell Command Prompt Git Bash Change the setting and open a new terminal tab for it to take effect. Each tab is an independent session. Use the + button on the terminal tab bar to spawn another. Close the active tab from the tab context menu or Terminal → Kill Current Terminal . Closing the panel does not kill sessions. New terminals start in the open project folder. If no folder is open, Shape prompts you to open one first. Select text to copy. Enable Copy on Select in terminal settings if you prefer automatic copy on highlight. Scrollback buffer size is configurable in Terminal Settings. When AI proposes a terminal command, approving it runs in the integrated terminal. Output appears in the same panel. NPM Scripts Terminal Settings Titlebar and Panels Problems, Output, and Tests

pages.title: NPM Scripts
pages.description: Run package.json scripts from the titlebar without typing commands.
pages.body: When your project has a package.json with a scripts section, Shape surfaces those scripts in the titlebar Scripts dropdown. 1. Open a project folder that contains package.json . 2. Click Scripts in the titlebar (right side). 3. Choose a script (for example dev , build , lint ). Shape runs the equivalent of npm run (or your configured package manager) in the integrated terminal and opens the bottom panel if it was hidden. Shape detects the package manager from lockfiles and Settings → Node.js & NPM : Lockfile Default manager bun.lock Bun pnpm lock.yaml pnpm yarn.lock Yarn package lock.json npm Override with the Package Manager setting if needed. Stdout and stderr appear in the terminal tab. Long running scripts like dev keep the tab open until you stop the process with Ctrl+C . The Scripts button appears only when: A folder is open package.json exists at the project root The scripts object has at least one entry Monorepos with scripts in subpackages still run from the root package.json . Use the terminal for workspace specific commands. Integrated Terminal Titlebar and Panels Settings Overview First Project Tutorial

pages.title: Problems, Output, and Tests
pages.description: View diagnostics, tool logs, and test results in the bottom panel.
pages.body: Beyond the terminal, the bottom panel hosts tabs for diagnostics and tool output. Use them to track errors while you code. The Problems tab aggregates diagnostics from language servers, ESLint, and design checks. Action Shortcut Open Problems Ctrl+Shift+M or command palette View: Show Problems Next problem F8 Previous problem Shift+F8 Click a row to jump to the file and line. The status bar also shows error and warning counts when problems exist. TypeScript and JavaScript (LSP) ESLint (when enabled in settings) Design diagnostics (contrast and accessibility) CSS and HTML language services Fix issues in the editor or use Quick Fix ( Ctrl+. ) when available. The Output tab shows logs from Shape tooling and language servers. Open it from the command palette: View: Show Output . Use Output when diagnosing why a language service failed to start or when an extension like feature prints status messages. When test integration is available for your project, results appear in the Tests tab. Failed tests link to the asserting file. Run tests from the terminal ( npm test , etc.) or from task configurations. Shape surfaces structured results when the runner reports them. 1. Keep Problems visible while fixing a type error batch. 2. Switch to Terminal to run builds after fixes. 3. Check Output if Problems does not explain a missing language feature. Toggle the whole panel with Ctrl+ without losing tab contents. IntelliSense Lint and LSP Integrated Terminal Titlebar and Panels

pages.title: Settings Overview
pages.description: Open the settings editor and navigate categories for editor, Git, AI, and more.
pages.body: Shape stores preferences in a settings editor that opens as a tab in the workbench. Changes apply immediately or on the next relevant action. Click the gear icon on the activity bar Click Settings in the titlebar File → Preferences → Settings or Ctrl+, Close the settings tab with Ctrl+W like any editor tab. Category What it controls Editor Font, tabs, minimap, auto save, formatting Appearance UI zoom level Terminal Shell, font, scrollback Git Auto fetch, commit confirmation, blame AI Models, context, rules, MCP, indexing Files Exclude patterns, line endings Lint & Format ESLint and Prettier Languages & LSP Per language servers Node.js & NPM Interpreter, package manager Design Tools Tailwind controls, design autocomplete Select a category from the left sidebar. Settings in each section use toggles, dropdowns, and text fields. Settings are saved locally on your machine. They apply to all projects unless a project specific tool config overrides them (for example .prettierrc ). Individual settings can be restored by selecting the default value in each control. There is no single "reset all" button. Reinstalling Shape does not remove your saved settings file. Editor Settings Git Settings Terminal Settings AI Settings

pages.title: Editor Settings
pages.description: Configure font, display, tabs, auto-save, and formatting in the Monaco editor.
pages.body: Settings → Editor controls how code looks and behaves in the Monaco editor. Setting Description Font family Monospace face (presets plus custom) Font size Editor text size in pixels Font ligatures Enable programming ligatures Minimap Right edge code overview Line numbers On, off, or relative Render whitespace None, selection, or all Line highlight Highlight active line, gutter, both, or none Bracket pair colorization Color matched brackets Indent guides Vertical indent lines Bracket guides Vertical lines for bracket pairs Setting Description Tab size Spaces per tab stop Insert spaces Spaces instead of tab characters Detect indentation Read indent style from file content Setting Description Word wrap Off, on, or bounded column Cursor style Line, block, or underline Smooth scrolling Animated scroll Scroll beyond last line Extra space below file end Image preview Inline preview for image files Setting Description Auto save Off, after delay, or on focus change Auto save delay Milliseconds when using delay mode Format on save Run formatter when saving Trim trailing whitespace Remove trailing spaces on save Insert final newline Ensure file ends with newline Format on save uses Prettier when enabled and configured for the project. Some settings have keyboard shortcuts without opening settings: Action Shortcut Toggle word wrap Alt+Z Toggle minimap Command palette Editor: Toggle Minimap Format document Alt+Shift+F Editing Files Lint and LSP Settings Overview Design Tools

pages.title: Git Settings
pages.description: Configure auto-fetch, commit confirmation, and inline blame.
pages.body: Settings → Git controls how Shape's Source Control sidebar interacts with your repository. Setting Description Auto fetch Periodically run git fetch in the background Auto fetch interval Minutes between fetch cycles Auto fetch updates remote tracking branches so ahead/behind counts in the status bar stay current. It does not merge changes into your working branch. Confirm before commit shows a confirmation dialog when you click Commit. Enable it if you want an extra check before creating commits. Disable it for faster commits when you are confident in your staged changes. Git blame annotates lines in the editor with the last commit author and date. Enable blame in settings, then use the command palette or editor context to toggle blame decorations for the active file. Blame helps during code review and when tracing when a line changed. It requires an open Git repository. Branch creation, remote URLs, and push/pull actions live in the Source Control sidebar and Branches and Remotes docs, not in settings. GitHub authentication is managed from the avatar menu. Source Control Branches and Remotes Settings Overview Diff and Merge

pages.title: Terminal Settings
pages.description: Choose your default shell, font, and scrollback for the integrated terminal.
pages.body: Settings → Terminal configures the integrated terminal in the bottom panel. Default shell selects which program opens for new terminal tabs: Option Shell Auto Windows default (usually PowerShell) PowerShell Windows PowerShell Command Prompt cmd.exe Git Bash Bash from Git for Windows Existing tabs keep their shell. Open a New Terminal ( Ctrl+Shift+ ) after changing this setting. Setting Description Font family Monospace font for terminal text Font size Terminal text size Terminal font is independent from the editor font. Match them in Editor Settings if you prefer a unified look. Scrollback sets how many lines of output the terminal retains. Higher values help when reviewing long build logs. Very large buffers use more memory. Presets range from a few thousand lines to much larger histories. When Copy on Select is enabled, highlighting text in the terminal copies it to the clipboard automatically. Disable it if you prefer explicit Ctrl+C copy. The terminal inherits your system PATH and user environment variables. Install tools like Node.js and Git at the OS level, then restart Shape so new tabs pick them up. Integrated Terminal NPM Scripts Settings Overview Install

pages.title: Lint and LSP
pages.description: Enable ESLint, Prettier, and language servers for diagnostics and formatting.
pages.body: Shape bundles language tooling for web projects. Settings → Lint & Format and Settings → Languages & LSP control diagnostics and formatters. Setting Description Enable ESLint Run ESLint on supported files Fix on save Apply auto fixable rules when saving ESLint reads your project's config ( .eslintrc , eslint.config.js , etc.). Errors appear in the editor and Problems panel. Setting Description Enable Prettier Use Prettier as the document formatter When enabled, Format Document ( Alt+Shift+F ) and format on save use Prettier with project config ( .prettierrc , prettier.config.js ). Toggle built in language services under Languages & LSP : Server Languages TypeScript .ts , .tsx , .js , .jsx CSS .css , modules HTML .html JSON .json , .jsonc Tailwind CSS Class completions in markup Emmet HTML/CSS abbreviations Disabling a server stops its diagnostics and completions for that language. Settings → Node.js & NPM includes Coding assistance for JavaScript tooling integration. Keep it enabled for npm package IntelliSense in import paths. Design autocomplete and diagnostics live under Settings → Design Tools , not LSP. See Design Tools. If diagnostics never appear: 1. Confirm the language server toggle is on. 2. Open Problems ( Ctrl+Shift+M ) for silent errors. 3. Check Output via the command palette for server startup logs. 4. Ensure the project has the expected config files ( tsconfig.json , ESLint config). Languages and tooling IntelliSense Problems, Output, and Tests Editor Settings Settings Overview

pages.title: First Project
pages.description: Open a web project, run the dev server, and make your first edit in Shape.
pages.body: This tutorial walks through opening an existing web project, running it locally, and saving a small change. It assumes Shape is installed on Windows. 1. Launch Shape. 2. Click Open Project on the welcome screen (or File → Open Folder , Ctrl+K Ctrl+O ). 3. Select a folder that contains a package.json (your own app or a cloned repo). The Explorer sidebar lists project files. Click package.json to inspect scripts and dependencies. 1. Open the terminal with Ctrl+ or the titlebar panel toggle. 2. Run your package manager install command: Use pnpm install , yarn , or bun install if that is what the project expects. Wait for install to finish before starting the dev server. Option A: click Scripts in the titlebar and choose dev (or start ). Option B: type in the terminal: The terminal shows the local URL (often http://localhost:3000 or similar). Open it in your browser to confirm the app runs. 1. Press Ctrl+P and type the name of a component or page file. 2. Make a visible change (for example edit a heading string). 3. Save with Ctrl+S . The browser should hot reload if the dev server supports it. Press Ctrl+Shift+M to open the Problems panel. Fix any TypeScript or ESLint issues the project reports. 1. Open AI Chat from the titlebar. 2. Select Ask mode. 3. Ask: "What does the main entry file do?" Review the answer without applying edits. Sign in with a Shape account if prompted. Open folders and navigate with Ctrl+P Run scripts from the titlebar or terminal Save files and read diagnostics Ask questions in read only AI mode Quick Start NPM Scripts Chat Overview Editing Files

pages.title: Refactor with AI
pages.description: Use Plan and Code modes to rename a pattern and review each proposed change.
pages.body: This tutorial shows a safe AI assisted refactor: extract a repeated utility, update call sites, and review every diff before accepting. 1. Open a project folder in Shape. 2. Sign in to your Shape account for AI access. 3. Open AI Chat from the titlebar. Pick a small, well scoped task, such as "Move duplicated date formatting into lib/format date.ts and update imports." For larger refactors, start in Plan mode: 1. Select Plan from the mode dropdown. 2. Describe the refactor and which files you think are involved. 3. Send the message. The assistant researches the codebase and saves a plan to .shape/plans/ . Open that file in the editor, edit if needed, then continue in Code mode. 1. Switch the dropdown to Code . 2. Send a clear instruction, for example: Create lib/format date.ts with a formatDate function. Replace inline toLocaleDateString calls in components/ with imports from the new module. Do not change unrelated files. 3. Wait for the assistant to propose edits. Each changed file appears as a card in the chat thread. 1. Click Preview to open a diff tab. 2. Read added and removed lines. 3. Click Accept only when the change looks correct. 4. Click Reject on anything that touches files outside scope. Do not enable auto apply until you are comfortable with the workflow. See Reviewing Edits. After accepting edits: 1. Save all files ( Ctrl+K S ). 2. Open Problems ( Ctrl+Shift+M ) and fix new type errors. 3. Run tests or the dev server from the terminal: If the assistant proposed a terminal command, approve Run on the card and check output in the panel. If something failed, send a follow up in the same thread: The test in format date.test.ts fails because of timezone. Fix the test to use UTC. Review and accept the follow up edits the same way. Use Plan for design and Code for implementation Preview and accept edits one file at a time Verify with Problems and terminal commands Chat Modes Reviewing Edits Diff and Merge Problems, Output, and Tests

pages.title: Clone and Commit
pages.description: Clone a GitHub repository, make a change, and push a commit from Shape.
pages.body: This tutorial covers cloning a repository, committing a change, and pushing to GitHub using Shape's Git UI. 1. Click Clone Repository . 2. Paste a Git URL, for example https://github.com/org/repo.git . 3. Choose a parent folder on disk. Shape runs git clone in the terminal. After cloning, open the new folder with File → Open Folder and select the repository directory. For HTTPS remotes, sign in with GitHub from the avatar menu before pushing. This avoids repeated credential prompts. Your Shape account (for AI) and GitHub sign in are separate. See Accounts. 1. Open a file from the Explorer. 2. Edit and save ( Ctrl+S ). 3. Open Source Control ( Ctrl+Shift+G ). The file appears under Changes . Click it to open a diff tab and review what changed. 1. Click + next to the file to stage it (or stage all from the Changes header). 2. Enter a commit message, for example docs: fix typo in readme . 3. Click Commit . Optional: click the sparkle icon for an AI suggested commit message from your diff. 1. Check the current branch in the Source Control header. 2. Click Push (up arrow) in the toolbar. 3. If prompted, complete GitHub authentication. Use Sync to pull remote changes first when the status bar shows you are behind the remote. Open Git Graph from the activity bar to see your commit in the lane diagram. Right click it to inspect files or compare with the working tree. Issue Fix Authentication failed Sign out and sign in again from the avatar GitHub menu Rejected non fast forward Click Pull , resolve conflicts if any, then push No remote configured Add origin in the remotes dialog. See Branches and Remotes Clone from the welcome screen Stage, commit, and push from Source Control Use Git Graph to confirm history Source Control GitHub Sign In Branches and Remotes Git Graph

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Fix common install, sign-in, and AI issues.
pages.body: Use Windows 10 or 11 (64 bit). Download again from Download or GitHub releases. 1. Finish sign in in the browser when prompted. 2. Sign out and sign in again from the avatar menu. See Accounts. Check your plan and credits on Billing. Free tier cannot use all paid models. Install FAQ Contact support

pages.title: Contact support
pages.description: How to reach the Shape team.
pages.body: Use the contact page for billing, account, or product questions. Include your account email, OS, and Shape version ( Help → About ). Do not send passwords or API keys. Report security issues privately via SECURITY.md, or use the contact form with topic Security . FAQ Troubleshooting

pages.title: Error codes
pages.description: Numeric Shape error codes for the cloud and the IDE.
pages.body: Code Area Name 1000 Account Auth required 1001 Account Offline 1002 Account Session expired 1003 Account Sign in failed 2000 Cloud AI AI provider failure 2001 Cloud AI Usage or credits 2002 Cloud AI Network timeout 2003 Cloud AI Payment required 2100 Cloud AI Rate limited 3000 Client Unofficial build 4000 IDE Workspace or file access 4100 IDE Git failed 4200 IDE Language server 4300 IDE Index or search 4400 IDE Terminal 4500 IDE Update failed 9000 General Unknown error Troubleshooting Contact support

pages.title: 1002 Session expired
pages.description: Your Shape session is no longer valid.
pages.body: Your account session expired, was revoked, or you signed out elsewhere. 1. Sign in again from the app or login. 2. If you changed your password or enabled 2FA, complete the new challenge. 3. If it keeps happening, revoke sessions in the dashboard and sign in once. 1000 Auth required Contact support

pages.title: 1003 Sign-in failed
pages.description: Shape could not complete desktop or browser sign-in.
pages.body: Sign in did not finish. The browser flow may have failed, timed out, or returned an error. 1. Try Sign in again from the app. 2. Complete login in the browser window that opens, then return to Shape. 3. Check that you can reach useshape.org and that you have an invite if signup is required. 4. If it keeps failing, sign in on the dashboard first, then retry from the app. 1000 Auth required Accounts Contact support

pages.title: 2003 Payment required
pages.description: Your subscription payment failed or is past due.
pages.body: Payment for your plan failed, or the subscription is past due. Local editing still works. Premium AI is paused until billing is current. 1. Open Billing. 2. Choose Manage billing and update your card. 3. Pay any open invoice in the portal, or wait for Stripe to retry. 2001 Usage or credits Contact support

pages.title: 2100 Rate limited
pages.description: The AI service asked you to slow down.
pages.body: Too many AI requests were sent in a short time. The provider or Shape Cloud asked you to wait. 1. Wait a short time, then send the message again. 2. Avoid rapidly retrying the same request. 3. If this happens often on a paid plan, check billing and contact support. 2000 AI provider failure 2001 Usage or credits Models and Pricing

pages.title: 4000 Workspace or file access
pages.description: Shape could not read or write a path in your project.
pages.body: The editor, agent, or a tool could not access a file or folder. Common causes: missing permissions, a deleted file, or a path outside the open workspace. 1. Confirm the folder still exists and you can edit it. 2. Re open the project in Shape. 3. On Windows, check whether antivirus is locking files. 4. If an agent used a path outside the workspace, reject it and ask again with an in project path. Troubleshooting Contact support

pages.title: 4100 Git failed
pages.description: A Git operation failed in Shape.
pages.body: Shape could not complete a Git action (status, commit, push, pull, branch, or fetch). Common causes: bad credentials, no remote, a locked .git/index.lock , or merge conflicts. 1. Confirm the folder is a Git repo and you have a remote if you are pushing. 2. If you see a lock error, close other Git tools and delete a stale .git/index.lock only when no Git process is running. 3. Sign in to GitHub from Shape if the remote needs auth. 4. Resolve merge conflicts, then retry. Source control GitHub sign in Troubleshooting

pages.title: 4200 Language server
pages.description: A language server failed to start or crashed.
pages.body: IntelliSense, go to definition, or diagnostics stopped because a language server exited or never started. Editing still works; language features may be limited. 1. Re open the file or the project folder. 2. Check Settings → Languages and confirm the server for this file type is enabled. 3. For TypeScript/JavaScript, ensure node modules (or your toolchain) is installed. 4. Watch Output → LSP for the underlying message, then retry. IntelliSense Language servers Troubleshooting

pages.title: 4300 Index or search
pages.description: Project search or codebase indexing failed.
pages.body: File search, content search, or AI codebase indexing could not run. Causes include a missing search binary, a corrupt index, or a folder Shape cannot read. 1. Confirm the project folder is still open and readable. 2. Retry search, or re run indexing from Settings → AI . 3. On Windows, check antivirus exclusions for the project and Shape install. 4. If content search mentions ripgrep, reinstall Shape or ensure the bundled search tool is present. Workspace search Indexing and search Troubleshooting

pages.title: 4400 Terminal
pages.description: The integrated terminal failed to start or run a command.
pages.body: Shape could not open a terminal session or run a shell command. Often the configured shell path is wrong, missing, or blocked by policy. 1. Open Settings and confirm your default shell path. 2. Try launching the same shell outside Shape. 3. On Windows, prefer a full path to powershell.exe or cmd.exe if PATH is incomplete. 4. Re open the terminal tab after fixing the shell. Integrated terminal Troubleshooting

pages.title: 4500 Update failed
pages.description: Shape could not check for or install an update.
pages.body: Checking for updates, downloading, or installing a new Shape build failed. 1. Try Help → Check for Updates again. 2. Confirm you are online and can reach Shape’s update servers. 3. If install keeps failing, download the latest installer from download and run it manually. Installing Shape Contact support

pages.title: Auth required
pages.description: Error 1000: sign in is required to continue.
pages.body: Error 1000: Auth required You need to be signed in to your Shape account for this action. 1. Sign in from Settings → Account, or from the titlebar account menu. 2. If sign in fails, complete the browser flow and return to the app. 3. Sign out and sign in again if your session expired. Accounts Error codes Contact Support

pages.title: Offline
pages.description: Error 1001: Shape could not reach its servers.
pages.body: Error 1001: Offline Shape could not reach its servers. This is usually a network problem or a temporary service interruption. 1. Check that you are online and that firewalls or VPNs are not blocking Shape. 2. Wait a moment and try again if the service may be temporarily unavailable. 3. Confirm the Shape website loads in your browser. Local editing still works offline. Account sync and AI features need a connection. Troubleshooting Error codes Contact Support

pages.title: AI provider failure
pages.description: Error 2000: the model provider returned an error.
pages.body: Error 2000: AI provider failure The model provider returned an error while handling your request. 1. Retry the request after a short wait. 2. Switch to a different model and try again. 3. Check status and billing if failures continue across models. Models and Pricing Error codes Contact Support

pages.title: Usage or credits
pages.description: Error 2001: a usage or credit limit was reached.
pages.body: Error 2001: Usage or credits You have reached a usage or credit limit for this request. 1. Check your plan and remaining credits on the billing page. 2. Use Auto if you are on the free tier, or wait for monthly Auto allowance to reset. 3. Upgrade your plan if you need more premium model capacity. Models and Pricing Pricing Error codes Contact Support

pages.title: Network timeout
pages.description: Error 2002: a network or timeout error interrupted the request.
pages.body: Error 2002: Network timeout A network or timeout error interrupted the request before it completed. 1. Check your connection and retry. 2. Disable or adjust VPN / proxy settings if requests fail only from this network. 3. Try again later if the path to Shape or the model provider is unstable. Troubleshooting Error codes Contact Support

pages.title: Official build required
pages.description: Error 3000: Shape Cloud AI needs an official release.
pages.body: Error 3000: Official build required Shape Cloud AI only accepts official Shape releases. Local editing, Git, and tooling still work in any build. 1. Install Shape from download. 2. Open the official app (not a custom or fork build) and sign in again. Installing Shape Error codes

pages.title: Unknown error
pages.description: Error 9000: an unexpected error occurred.
pages.body: Error 9000: Unknown error An unexpected error occurred that does not match a more specific Shape error code. 1. Retry the action. 2. Restart Shape if the problem persists. 3. Contact support with the error code and what you were doing. Troubleshooting Error codes Contact Support

chunks.text: Windows 10 or later (64 bit) Git (for clone and source control) Node.js (recommended for scripts and language tooling) You can open local projects without an account. Sign in is required for cloud AI.

chunks.heading: Install
chunks.text: 1. Download the Windows installer from useshape.org/download. 2. Run the installer. If Windows SmartScreen warns that the app is unrecognized, choose More info , then Run anyway (common for new release hashes). 3. Open Shape from the Start menu.
chunks.title: Installing Shape

chunks.heading: First check
chunks.text: 1. File → Open Folder and pick a project. 2. Open the terminal ( View → Terminal or Ctrl+ ). If both work, you are set. Continue with Quick Start.

chunks.heading: Updates
chunks.text: Shape checks for updates automatically. Use Help → Check for Updates , or follow the titlebar prompt when one is available. In Settings → Account , switch the update channel to Pre release or turn off automatic checks.

chunks.text: Shape will not start Restart Windows and try again. Re run the installer. Check that antivirus is not blocking Shape. Git or Node missing in the terminal Install Git for Windows and Node.js, then restart Shape.

chunks.heading: 1. Open a project
chunks.text: File → Open Folder , or use Ctrl+K Ctrl+O . Pick the folder that contains your code. The Explorer lists files; click one to open it in the editor. To clone instead: use Clone Repository on the welcome screen, paste a Git URL, and choose a parent folder.

chunks.text: Action Shortcut Command palette Ctrl+Shift+P Quick open file Ctrl+P Find in project Ctrl+Shift+F Toggle terminal Ctrl+ Open settings Ctrl+, Toggle AI chat Ctrl+L If you forget a shortcut, search for the action in the command palette.

chunks.heading: 4. Try AI chat
chunks.text: Open the chat panel and send a question about the open project. Use @ mentions to attach files, folders, the codebase, or the current selection. Review proposed edits in the chat UI before applying them. See Chat overview and Chat modes.

chunks.text: The workbench is Shape's main editing surface. Everything you do, from editing files to running Git and chatting with AI, happens inside this layout.
chunks.title: Workbench Tour

chunks.heading: Layout overview
chunks.text: Shape divides the window into five regions: Activity bar : narrow strip on the far left; switches sidebar views Primary sidebar : file tree, search, Git, outline, and more Editor : tabbed Monaco code area in the center Secondary sidebar : AI chat on the right Bottom panel : terminal and diagnostic views
chunks.title: Workbench Tour

chunks.heading: Titlebar
chunks.text: The titlebar holds: Menus : File, Edit, View, Go, Terminal, Window, Help Sidebar toggle : show or hide the primary sidebar Scripts dropdown : npm scripts for the open project Panel toggle : terminal and bottom views AI Chat toggle : right sidebar Settings and Reset Layout buttons Avatar menu : Shape account and GitHub sign in Drag the titlebar to move the window (on Windows, outside the menu buttons).
chunks.title: Workbench Tour

chunks.heading: When no project is open
chunks.text: Without a folder open, the editor area shows the welcome screen with Open Project, Clone Repository, Terminal, and AI Chat shortcuts. See Quick Start.
chunks.title: Workbench Tour

chunks.heading: When a project is open
chunks.text: With a folder open but no file selected, the center prompts you to pick a file from the Explorer or press Ctrl+P .
chunks.title: Workbench Tour

chunks.heading: Collapsing regions
chunks.text: Every major region can be hidden for focus: Region How to toggle Primary sidebar Titlebar sidebar button, or click the active activity bar icon again Bottom panel Titlebar panel button, View → Terminal , or Ctrl+ AI chat Titlebar chat button, or View → AI Chat All chrome Zen Mode with Ctrl+K Z Use Reset Layout in the titlebar to restore the default arrangement.
chunks.title: Workbench Tour

chunks.heading: Settings and release notes as tabs
chunks.text: Settings and Keyboard Shortcuts open as editor tabs instead of separate windows when launched from the activity bar or menu. Close them like any other tab with Ctrl+W .

chunks.text: The activity bar is the vertical strip on the far left of the workbench. Each icon opens a different view in the primary sidebar .
chunks.title: Activity Bar

chunks.heading: Sidebar views
chunks.text: Icon View Purpose File Explorer Browse and open project files Branch Source Control Stage, commit, and review changes Commit Git Graph Visual commit history List Outline Symbols in the active file Search Search Find and replace across the workspace Click an icon to switch views. Click the same icon again to collapse the sidebar entirely.
chunks.title: Activity Bar

chunks.heading: Dirty file badge
chunks.text: When you have unsaved files, the Explorer icon shows a small badge with the count of dirty tabs. Save with Ctrl+S or File → Save All to clear it.
chunks.title: Activity Bar

chunks.heading: Bottom actions
chunks.text: Below the view icons, the activity bar has two fixed buttons: Button Action Terminal icon Opens the Command Palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P ) Gear icon Opens Settings These are shortcuts, not sidebar views. Settings opens in an editor tab.
chunks.title: Activity Bar

chunks.heading: Opening views from the menu
chunks.text: Every activity bar view is also available from View in the menu bar: View → Explorer ( Ctrl+Shift+E ) View → Search ( Ctrl+Shift+F ) View → Source Control ( Ctrl+Shift+G ) View → Git Graph View → Outline Use whichever path fits your workflow.
chunks.title: Activity Bar

chunks.heading: What is not on the activity bar
chunks.text: Some features live elsewhere: AI Chat : titlebar toggle or View → AI Chat (right sidebar) Terminal : bottom panel, not the activity bar Problems / Output : bottom panel tabs Bookmarks : keyboard only ( Ctrl+Alt+B ); no activity bar entry
chunks.title: Activity Bar

chunks.heading: Left: menus and sidebar toggle
chunks.text: App icon : branding (Windows) Sidebar toggle : show or hide the primary sidebar Menu bar : File, Edit, View, Go, Terminal, Window, Help On narrow windows, overflow menus collapse into a ⋯ menu so critical items stay reachable.

chunks.text: When a file is open, the center shows the project path and filename. This region is draggable for window movement.

chunks.text: Control Function Scripts Run npm scripts from package.json Panel Toggle the bottom panel (terminal, problems) AI Chat Toggle the right sidebar Settings Open Settings tab Reset Layout Restore default panel sizes Avatar Shape account and GitHub sign in

chunks.heading: Bottom panel
chunks.text: The bottom panel stacks tabbed views: Tab Opens from Purpose Terminal View → Terminal , Ctrl+ , panel toggle Shell in project directory Problems View → Problems , Ctrl+Shift+M , command palette ESLint, TypeScript, and LSP diagnostics Output Command palette View: Show Output Tool and extension logs Tests Test runner integration Test results when available Click a tab to switch views. Drag the top edge of the panel to resize it.

chunks.heading: Scripts dropdown
chunks.text: When a package.json with a scripts section is in the open project, the Scripts button appears in the titlebar. 1. Click Scripts . 2. Choose a script (for example dev , build , test ). 3. Shape runs it in the integrated terminal and opens the panel if needed. See NPM Scripts for details.
chunks.title: Titlebar and Panels

chunks.heading: Panel vs sidebar
chunks.text: Primary sidebar (left): persistent project tools like files, Git, and search Secondary sidebar (right): AI chat Bottom panel : transient command output like terminal, problems, and tests Toggling the panel does not close your terminal session. It hides the panel until you show it again.
chunks.title: Titlebar and Panels

chunks.heading: Reset Layout
chunks.text: If panels feel misplaced or too small, click Reset Layout (desktop windows icon) in the titlebar. This restores: Primary sidebar open Bottom panel open AI chat closed It does not close open files or change your project.
