chunks.text: The command palette is Shape's universal action search. Open it with Ctrl+Shift+P or from View → Command Palette… . Type to filter commands. Press Enter to run the selected action, or Escape to close.
chunks.title: Command Palette

chunks.heading: Default mode
chunks.text: In default mode, the palette lists: Workbench commands : panels, settings, chat history, zen mode Editor commands from the active file: format, rename, fold, comment Commands show keyboard shortcuts on the right when assigned. Fuzzy matching works on both label and shortcut fragments. You can also open the palette from the activity bar bottom button (terminal icon).
chunks.title: Command Palette

chunks.heading: Files mode (Ctrl+P)
chunks.text: Go to File opens a dedicated files mode, not the full command list. 1. Press Ctrl+P (or Go → Go to File… ). 2. Type part of a filename. 3. Press Enter to open the match. This mode is optimized for speed. In Shape, Ctrl+Shift+P and Ctrl+P are separate shortcuts.
chunks.title: Command Palette

chunks.heading: Go to line (Ctrl+G)
chunks.text: Jump to a specific line (and optionally column): 1. Press Ctrl+G ( Go → Go to Line/Column… ). 2. Type a line number, or line:column (for example 42:8 ). 3. Press Enter . The editor scrolls and places the cursor at that position.
chunks.title: Command Palette

chunks.heading: Workspace symbols (Ctrl+T)
chunks.text: Find functions, classes, and variables across the project: 1. Press Ctrl+T or run Go to Symbol in Workspace… from the palette. 2. Type a symbol name. 3. Select a result to open the defining file at that location. Indexing quality depends on language support and LSP configuration. See IntelliSense.
chunks.title: Command Palette

chunks.heading: Chat history mode
chunks.text: Browse past AI conversations: 1. Open the command palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P ). 2. Run Chat: Show History . 3. Select a conversation to reopen it in the AI sidebar. Useful when you need to continue an earlier thread without scrolling the chat panel.
chunks.title: Command Palette

chunks.heading: Language mode
chunks.text: Change syntax highlighting for the active file: 1. Open the palette and run Change Language Mode… . 2. Pick a language from the filtered list (TypeScript, Markdown, CSS, etc.). Shape remembers the association for that file path. Language mode affects highlighting, snippets, and LSP behavior.
chunks.title: Command Palette

chunks.heading: Tips
chunks.text: Quick Fix ( Ctrl+. ) is an editor action, not the palette, but you can find it by typing quick fix in the palette. Palette only commands (no default shortcut) include View: Show Problems , View: Show Output , Editor: Toggle Minimap , and Chat: Show History . When the palette is open, arrow keys navigate. Typing immediately filters.

chunks.heading: Primary sidebar (left)
chunks.text: Open : click any activity bar icon, or use View → Explorer (etc.) Close : click the active activity bar icon again, or use the titlebar sidebar toggle Resize : drag the divider between sidebar and editor The sidebar remembers which view was active (Explorer, Search, Git, etc.).

chunks.heading: Reset Layout
chunks.text: Click Reset Layout in the titlebar (desktop windows icon) to restore defaults: Region Default state Primary sidebar Open Bottom panel Open Secondary sidebar (AI) Closed Reset does not affect open files, Zen Mode preference, or sidebar view selection.

chunks.heading: Zen Mode
chunks.text: Zen Mode hides the activity bar, both sidebars, and the bottom panel, leaving only the editor and titlebar menus.

chunks.heading: Enter or exit
chunks.text: View → Zen Mode Command palette: View: Toggle Zen Mode Ctrl+K Z (chord: press Ctrl+K , release, then Z ) Press the same shortcut again to exit. Your panel open/closed state is restored.

chunks.heading: When to use Zen Mode
chunks.text: Writing or reviewing a long file without sidebar noise Presenting code in a meeting Pairing where chat and Git panels are not needed temporarily Zen Mode does not change font size or word wrap. Adjust those in Editor Settings.
chunks.title: Layout and Zen Mode

chunks.heading: Split editor
chunks.text: For side by side editing, use the tab bar split actions (see Tabs and Splits). Splits work inside Zen Mode. Only chrome is hidden, not multi group editing.

chunks.text: The Shape editor is built on Monaco, the same engine that powers VS Code. It provides syntax highlighting, multi cursor editing, and language aware features for web projects.
chunks.title: Editing Files

chunks.heading: Open and create files
chunks.text: Action Menu Shortcut Open file File → Open File Ctrl+O Open folder File → Open Folder Ctrl+K Ctrl+O New file File → New Text File Ctrl+N Quick open Go → Go to File… Ctrl+P New files from File → New Text File appear in the Explorer when saved. New Scratch File creates a temporary buffer without a path until you save.
chunks.title: Editing Files

chunks.heading: Save and close
chunks.text: Action Shortcut Save Ctrl+S Save As Ctrl+Shift+S Save All Ctrl+K S Close tab Ctrl+W Close all tabs Ctrl+K E Dirty tabs show a dot indicator. The Explorer activity bar badge counts unsaved files.

chunks.heading: Basic editing
chunks.text: Standard text operations work as expected: Undo / Redo : Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Cut / Copy / Paste : Ctrl+X / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V Select All : Ctrl+A
chunks.title: Editing Files

chunks.heading: Multi-cursor
chunks.text: Hold Alt and click to add cursors. Use Ctrl+Alt+↑ and Ctrl+Alt+↓ to add cursors on adjacent lines. Ctrl+Shift+L selects all occurrences of the current selection.

chunks.heading: Navigation within a file
chunks.text: Go to Line : Ctrl+G Go to Definition : F12 (requires language support) Go to Bracket : Ctrl+Shift+\\ Back / Forward : Alt+Left / Alt+Right through cursor history

chunks.text: Toggle wrap from View → Word Wrap or the command palette ( Editor: Toggle Word Wrap , Alt+Z ).

chunks.text: Shape opens every file in a tab at the top of the editor. Tabs support preview modes, split groups, and quick navigation across your working set.
chunks.title: Tabs and Splits

chunks.heading: Opening and closing tabs
chunks.text: Action Shortcut Close active tab Ctrl+W Close all tabs Ctrl+K E Reopen closed tab Command palette: Reopen Closed Editor Dirty tabs show a dot on the label. Save with Ctrl+S before closing if you want to keep changes. Click a tab to switch files. Middle click a tab (or use the close icon) to close it.
chunks.title: Tabs and Splits

chunks.heading: Split editor
chunks.text: Split the editor to view two files side by side: 1. Click the Split Editor Right button on the tab bar, or use the tab context menu. 2. The active file moves to the right group. The left group keeps its previous file. 3. Click Close Split to return to a single group. Each split group has its own tab strip and active file. Drag tabs between groups when both are visible. Splits work in Zen Mode. Only sidebars are hidden, not multi group editing.
chunks.title: Tabs and Splits

chunks.heading: Preview modes
chunks.text: Some file types support alternate views from the tab bar toggle: File type Modes Markdown Source, split, and rendered preview Images Raw path and inline preview Fonts Source and live preview For Markdown, cycle through Source , Split View , and Preview with the toggle on the tab. Split view shows the editor and preview at the same time.
chunks.title: Tabs and Splits

chunks.heading: Diff tabs
chunks.text: Git changes open as special diff tabs labeled Working Tree or Index . These are read only comparison views. See Diff and Merge.
chunks.title: Tabs and Splits

chunks.heading: Pinning and ordering
chunks.text: Tabs reflect open order. The most recently used file becomes active when you click its tab or open it from the Explorer. Use Ctrl+P to jump between files without clicking tabs.

chunks.text: Shape renders Markdown files with a built in preview powered by the same tab you use for source editing. Switch between source, split, and preview without leaving the workbench.
chunks.title: Markdown Preview

chunks.heading: Open a Markdown file
chunks.text: Open any .md or .mdx file from the Explorer or with Ctrl+P . Syntax highlighting applies in source mode.
chunks.title: Markdown Preview

chunks.heading: Preview modes
chunks.text: Use the mode toggle on the tab bar to cycle views: Mode What you see Source Raw Markdown in the Monaco editor Split Editor on one side, rendered preview on the other Preview Full width rendered output Split view is useful when editing documentation and checking headings, links, and code blocks at the same time.
chunks.title: Markdown Preview

chunks.heading: What the preview supports
chunks.text: The preview renders standard Markdown elements: Headings, paragraphs, and lists Links and images (relative paths resolve from the file location) Fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting Blockquotes and inline formatting Complex MDX components used in Shape's own docs site may not render identically in the IDE preview. The preview targets common Markdown, not full MDX execution.
chunks.title: Markdown Preview

chunks.heading: Scroll and edit workflow
chunks.text: In split mode, edit on the left and confirm layout on the right. Save with Ctrl+S to persist changes. The preview updates when the file content changes.
chunks.title: Markdown Preview

chunks.heading: Tips
chunks.text: Use Ctrl+Shift+P and run Change Language Mode… if a file is not detected as Markdown. For long docs, Zen Mode plus split preview gives a focused writing surface. Pair preview with Bookmarks to jump between sections you are revising.

chunks.text: Shape shows file differences in dedicated diff tabs so you can review changes before committing or accepting AI edits.
chunks.title: Diff and Merge

chunks.heading: Git diff tabs
chunks.text: From Source Control , click a changed file to open a diff tab. Tabs are labeled with the filename and context: Label Meaning Working Tree Unstaged changes vs the index Index Staged changes vs the last commit The diff view uses Monaco's inline comparison with added and removed highlighting. Read the changes, then stage or discard from the Source Control sidebar.
chunks.title: Diff and Merge

chunks.heading: Open diffs from Git Graph
chunks.text: In the Git Graph, right click a commit and choose Compare with Working Tree or View Changes to inspect historical diffs.
chunks.title: Diff and Merge

chunks.heading: AI edit previews
chunks.text: When AI chat edits files in Code mode, each change appears as a review card after it is written to disk. 1. Click the file (or Preview ) to open a diff in the editor. 2. Compare the latest step against the previous version. 3. Keep leaves the file as written. Undo restores the baseline from before the unresolved edit chain. See Reviewing Edits for the full Keep/Undo workflow.
chunks.title: Diff and Merge

chunks.heading: Merge conflicts
chunks.text: If a git pull or merge produces conflicts, Shape surfaces conflict markers in the affected files. Open the file in the editor and look for standard conflict sections: Resolve conflicts manually in the editor, then stage the file and commit. Shape does not yet provide a dedicated three way merge UI. Use the diff tabs and editor for manual resolution.
chunks.title: Diff and Merge

chunks.heading: Tips
chunks.text: Close diff tabs with Ctrl+W when review is done. Unstaged and staged diffs open as separate tabs so you can compare both states. Enable Git: Blame in settings to see line attribution while reviewing changes.

chunks.text: Shape includes design aware tooling for web UI work. Completions, inline controls, and diagnostics help you edit Tailwind classes and CSS variables without leaving the editor.
chunks.title: Design Tools

chunks.heading: Tailwind inline controls
chunks.text: When your cursor is inside a className string, Shape can show inline controls for common utilities: Flex / Grid : direction, wrap, justify content, align items. Click the swatch next to a flex or grid token Gap : column and row gap. Click a gap token Padding : per side padding. Click a p / px / pl token Color picker : Tailwind palette and project CSS variables Controls appear as a floating panel near the attribute. Click a value to apply it directly to the source. Toggle controls in Settings → Design Tools → Tailwind Controls .
chunks.title: Design Tools

chunks.heading: Design autocomplete
chunks.text: Shape suggests Tailwind semantic tokens, CSS design variables, and in project class patterns while you type inside className attributes and style blocks. Enable or disable this in Settings → Design Tools → Design Autocomplete .
chunks.title: Design Tools

chunks.heading: Monorepo git and aliases
chunks.text: Opening a parent folder (for example a repo that contains shape/ and website/ as separate git roots) discovers each nested repository for Source Control and explorer decorations. Accessibility checks run on color contrast and related design issues in supported files (JSX, TSX, CSS). Violations appear as squiggles in the editor and in the Problems panel. Configure severity in Settings → Design Tools → Design Diagnostics . Choose AA or AAA contrast level.
chunks.title: Design Tools

chunks.heading: Color and CSS variables
chunks.text: The color picker reads from: Tailwind's default palette CSS variables defined in project files like design tokens.css Picking a color inserts the matching class or variable reference at the cursor.
chunks.title: Design Tools

chunks.heading: AI Design mode
chunks.text: The chat panel includes a Design mode tuned for UI and styling changes. It follows existing project patterns before introducing new styles. See Chat Modes.

chunks.text: IntelliSense is Shape's language aware assistance in the Monaco editor. Completions, hovers, diagnostics, and navigation come from built in language servers and editor services.
chunks.title: IntelliSense

chunks.heading: Completions
chunks.text: Start typing to see suggestions. Press Tab or Enter to accept. Shape enables language servers for common web stacks: Language Features TypeScript / JavaScript Types, imports, refactor hints CSS / HTML Selectors, tags, attributes JSON Schema aware keys and values Tailwind CSS Class name completions in className Toggle individual servers in Settings → Languages & LSP .
chunks.title: IntelliSense

chunks.heading: Quick Fix
chunks.text: When a diagnostic offers a fix, a lightbulb appears in the gutter. Press Ctrl+. to open Quick Fix and choose an action. Common fixes include adding imports, fixing ESLint violations, and applying TypeScript corrections.
chunks.title: IntelliSense

chunks.heading: Navigation
chunks.text: Action Shortcut Go to Definition F12 Peek Definition Alt+F12 Find All References Shift+F12 Go to Symbol in Workspace Ctrl+T Go to Next Problem F8 Go to Previous Problem Shift+F8 Go to Symbol in Editor is available from the command palette for symbols in the current file.
chunks.title: IntelliSense

chunks.heading: Hovers
chunks.text: Hover over a symbol to see type information, documentation, and color previews for CSS values. Hold Ctrl and hover a symbol to peek its definition inline.
chunks.title: IntelliSense

chunks.heading: Diagnostics
chunks.text: Errors and warnings appear as squiggles in the editor and aggregate in the Problems panel ( Ctrl+Shift+M ). Sources include: TypeScript compiler ESLint (when enabled) Design diagnostics for contrast issues Tailwind CSS language service Fix issues in the editor or open Problems to jump between files.
chunks.title: IntelliSense

chunks.heading: Rename symbol
chunks.text: Place the cursor on a symbol and press F2 to rename it across the project. Preview changes before confirming.

chunks.text: The Explorer header includes buttons to collapse all folders and refresh the tree. Refresh is useful after external tools add or remove files outside Shape.

chunks.text: The Search sidebar finds text across your entire workspace. Use it for refactors, auditing string usage, and locating config keys.
chunks.title: Workspace Search

chunks.heading: Open search
chunks.text: Click the search icon on the activity bar View → Search or Ctrl+Shift+F Edit → Find in Files from the menu
chunks.title: Workspace Search

chunks.heading: Find in files
chunks.text: 1. Type your search query in the search box. 2. Results appear grouped by file with line previews. 3. Click a result to open the file at that line. Search respects file exclude patterns from Settings → Files . Hidden folders like node modules are skipped by default.
chunks.title: Workspace Search

chunks.heading: Replace in files
chunks.text: Switch to replace mode with Ctrl+H or the toggle in the search sidebar. 1. Enter find and replace strings. 2. Review matches in the results list. 3. Replace one match at a time, or replace all in a file or across the workspace. Confirm bulk replacements carefully. Shape modifies files on disk when you apply a replace.
chunks.title: Workspace Search

chunks.heading: Search options
chunks.text: Use the buttons below the search field to toggle: Match case Match whole word Use regular expression Regex mode supports capture groups in replace strings.

chunks.text: The Outline sidebar lists symbols defined in the file you are editing. Use it to navigate long files without scrolling.

chunks.title: Outline

chunks.heading: What appears in the outline
chunks.text: Symbols depend on the file language and LSP support: Language Typical symbols TypeScript / JavaScript Functions, classes, interfaces, variables CSS Rules and selectors HTML Elements and sections Markdown Headings If symbols are missing, check that the correct language mode is set and the relevant LSP is enabled in Lint and LSP.

chunks.text: Click any entry to move the cursor to that symbol in the editor. The editor scrolls and focuses the definition. For project wide symbol search, use Ctrl+T ( Go to Symbol in Workspace ).

chunks.heading: Outline vs breadcrumbs
chunks.text: The titlebar breadcrumbs show the file path. The outline shows structure inside the file. Use both together when working in large modules.

chunks.text: Bookmarks let you save positions in code and return to them later. Bookmarks persist in local storage across sessions.
chunks.title: Bookmarks

chunks.heading: Toggle a bookmark
chunks.text: 1. Place the cursor on the line you want to mark. 2. Press Ctrl+Alt+B . A bookmark icon appears in the editor gutter. Press Ctrl+Alt+B again on the same line to remove it.
chunks.title: Bookmarks

chunks.heading: Navigate bookmarks
chunks.text: Action Shortcut Next bookmark Ctrl+F2 Previous bookmark Shift+F2 Navigation wraps around. If the next bookmark is in another file, Shape opens that file and moves the cursor.
chunks.title: Bookmarks

chunks.heading: View all bookmarks
chunks.text: Open the command palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P ) and search for Bookmarks to see the bookmark list panel. Each entry shows the file path, line number, and a short label. Click an entry to jump to that location. Remove bookmarks from the list when you no longer need them.
chunks.title: Bookmarks

chunks.heading: Labels
chunks.text: By default, bookmarks use the label Line N . When you toggle a bookmark on a word, Shape may use that word as the label.
chunks.title: Bookmarks

chunks.heading: Scope
chunks.text: Bookmarks are per workspace path and stored locally. They are not synced to Git or your Shape account. Clearing browser or app storage removes them.
chunks.title: Bookmarks

chunks.heading: Tips
chunks.text: Bookmark failing tests, TODO comments, or sections you revisit during a refactor. Bookmarks have no activity bar icon. Use keyboard shortcuts or the command palette. Combine with Outline for within file structure and bookmarks for cross file anchors.

Action How Stage one file Click the + icon next to the file Unstage Click the − icon on a staged file Stage all Click + on the Changes header Discard Right click and choose discard (confirm when prompted)

chunks.text: Shape exposes common branch and remote operations from the Source Control sidebar and branch picker. You rarely need a separate terminal for day to day Git workflow.
chunks.title: Branches and Remotes

chunks.heading: Current branch
chunks.text: The branch name appears at the top of Source Control and in the status bar. Click it to open the branch picker .
chunks.title: Branches and Remotes

chunks.heading: Switch branches
chunks.text: 1. Click the current branch name in Source Control. 2. Select a local branch from the list to check it out. 3. Shape runs git checkout and refreshes the file tree. Uncommitted changes may block checkout if they conflict. Commit or stash changes first.
chunks.title: Branches and Remotes

chunks.heading: Create a branch
chunks.text: From the branch picker: 1. Choose Create new branch… 2. Enter a name (for example feature/auth ). 3. Shape creates the branch from your current HEAD and checks it out. You can also create a branch from the command palette or integrated terminal if you prefer the CLI.
chunks.title: Branches and Remotes

chunks.heading: Remotes
chunks.text: Manage remotes from the Source Control toolbar or remote dialog: Action Description Add remote Link a name (usually origin ) to a URL Edit remote Change the URL for an existing remote Remove remote Delete the remote reference (not the server repo) Paste an HTTPS or SSH URL when adding a remote. For GitHub HTTPS remotes, sign in with GitHub to simplify authentication.
chunks.title: Branches and Remotes

chunks.heading: Fetch and sync
chunks.text: Pull downloads and merges remote changes into your current branch. Push uploads local commits the remote does not have yet. Sync runs pull then push. Enable Auto Fetch in Git Settings to refresh remote state on an interval.
chunks.title: Branches and Remotes

chunks.heading: Ahead and behind
chunks.text: After fetch, the status bar and branch picker may show counts like ↑2 ↓1 meaning you are two commits ahead and one behind the tracked remote branch. Push and pull to reconcile.

chunks.heading: Read the graph
chunks.text: Each row is a commit. Columns show: Lane lines : branch and merge topology Message : commit subject (click @mentions to open GitHub profiles) Author and relative time Expand a commit row to see files changed in that commit.

chunks.heading: Actions on commits

chunks.text: Use the search field at the top to filter commits by message or author. Clear the filter to show the full history again.

chunks.text: GitHub sign in lets Shape push and pull to GitHub without repeated password prompts. It is separate from your Shape account used for AI features.
chunks.title: GitHub Sign In

chunks.heading: When you need it
chunks.text: Sign in when you: Push commits to a GitHub HTTPS remote Pull from a private GitHub repository Want your GitHub username shown in the avatar menu Local Git operations (commit, branch, log) work without signing in.
chunks.title: GitHub Sign In

chunks.heading: Sign in
chunks.text: 1. Click the avatar in the titlebar. 2. Under GitHub , choose Sign in with GitHub . 3. Complete authorization in your browser. 4. Return to Shape. The menu shows @your username (GitHub) when connected. Shape stores credentials through Git's credential helper on Windows.
chunks.title: GitHub Sign In

chunks.heading: Sign out
chunks.text: Open the avatar menu → GitHub → Sign out . Your local repository data is unchanged. Only remote authentication is cleared.
chunks.title: GitHub Sign In

chunks.heading: Prerequisites
chunks.text: GitHub sign in requires Git tooling on your system: Git for Windows , or GitHub CLI If neither is installed, the avatar menu shows a note to install one. See Install for setup links.
chunks.title: GitHub Sign In

chunks.heading: Sign-in fails in the browser
chunks.text: Confirm you approved the Shape OAuth application. Check your network and try again from the avatar menu.
chunks.title: GitHub Sign In

chunks.heading: Push still asks for credentials
chunks.text: Verify the remote URL points to GitHub ( github.com ). Sign out and sign in again from the avatar menu. For SSH remotes, configure SSH keys outside Shape. GitHub sign in applies to HTTPS.
chunks.title: GitHub Sign In

chunks.heading: Wrong account
chunks.text: Sign out, then sign in with the correct GitHub account. Credential helpers may cache the previous user until you clear them.

Use @ mentions for a file, folder, the codebase, or the current editor selection.

chunks.text: Each chat message runs in a mode that controls what the assistant can do. Pick the mode from the dropdown next to the input box before you send.
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.heading: Mode reference
chunks.text: Mode Behavior Best for Ask Read only. No file edits or terminal commands. Learning the codebase, explaining errors Code Can read, edit, and run commands. Proposes changes for review. Implementing features and fixes Plan Research only. Writes a markdown plan to .shape/plans/ . Designing an approach before coding Design UI and styling focused. Follows existing design patterns. Layout, Tailwind, and component polish Review Systematic investigation of bugs, failures, and security issues, with an optional adversarial self check. Tracking down runtime/build errors, auditing auth, input handling, and dependencies
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.heading: Ask mode
chunks.text: Safe default for exploration. The assistant reads your project and answers questions but cannot modify files or run the terminal. Use Ask when onboarding to a new repo.
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.heading: Code mode
chunks.text: The default for implementation work. The assistant can: Read and search files Propose and apply edits shown as review cards (Keep / Undo) Run terminal commands (with your approval) Call finish when the task is done Switch to Code when you are ready to apply changes. See Reviewing Edits.
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.heading: Plan mode
chunks.text: Plan mode researches the codebase and saves an implementation plan as markdown under .shape/plans/ . Plans include a Todos checklist. It does not edit project source files. When the plan is ready, review the file and click Build this plan (or switch to Code and ask to implement). During build, the assistant maintains a live todo checklist in chat via update todos .
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.heading: Design mode
chunks.text: Design mode prioritizes existing UI conventions in your project. It is tuned for Tailwind classes, component structure, and visual consistency. Mention @design in chat when you want the assistant to focus on UI work. Pair with Design Tools in the editor.
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.heading: Review mode
chunks.text: Review mode combines systematic debugging with security minded review: it reads errors, logs, and relevant code before suggesting fixes, and watches for vulnerability patterns in auth flows, user input, and unsafe APIs. Enable the adversarial self check in AI settings to have a second pass challenge the first response before it's shown. Older Debug and Security selections are automatically migrated to Review — the two were folded into one mode.
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.heading: Switching modes
chunks.text: Change the mode between messages in the same thread. Earlier context carries over, but tool permissions follow the active mode for each new message.
chunks.title: Chat Modes

chunks.text: In Code mode (and other editing modes), the assistant can change files on disk as it works. Each change shows up for review so you can Keep it or Undo it.
chunks.title: Reviewing Edits

chunks.heading: How edits land
chunks.text: 1. The agent writes the updated file to disk. 2. Chat shows an edit card with +/ line counts for that step. 3. Open the file (or use Preview ) to review the diff in the editor. 4. Keep dismisses the review and leaves the file as written. 5. Undo restores the file to how it was before this unresolved edit chain. If the agent edits the same file again before you Keep or Undo, the review updates to the latest step. Undo restores the baseline from before the first unresolved edit on that file.
chunks.title: Reviewing Edits

chunks.heading: Edit cards
chunks.text: Each file change in the thread shows: The affected file path Added and removed line counts for that edit step Actions to open or review the change
chunks.title: Reviewing Edits

chunks.heading: Pending edits bar
chunks.text: When files still need a Keep or Undo decision, a summary appears above the chat input. Use Keep All or Undo All , or handle files one at a time.
chunks.title: Reviewing Edits

chunks.heading: Auto-apply
chunks.text: By default, edits still appear for review after they are written. Enable Auto Apply Edits in AI Settings to auto Keep proposals as they arrive. Use this only when you trust the workflow.
chunks.title: Reviewing Edits

chunks.heading: Terminal command approval
chunks.text: Separate from file edits, terminal commands show their own approval card. Click Run to execute in the integrated terminal or Reject to skip. The assistant cannot run shell commands without your approval.
chunks.title: Reviewing Edits

chunks.heading: Session persistence
chunks.text: Kept and undone edits are tracked for the conversation. Reloading the project preserves which proposals you already resolved. If the agent edits a file again after you Keep it, a new review opens for that later change.
chunks.title: Reviewing Edits

chunks.text: This tutorial walks through opening an existing web project, running it locally, and saving a small change. It assumes Shape is installed on Windows.

chunks.heading: Open the project
chunks.text: 1. Launch Shape. 2. Click Open Project on the welcome screen (or File → Open Folder , Ctrl+K Ctrl+O ). 3. Select a folder that contains a package.json (your own app or a cloned repo). The Explorer sidebar lists project files. Click package.json to inspect scripts and dependencies.
chunks.title: First Project

chunks.heading: Install dependencies
chunks.text: 1. Open the terminal with Ctrl+ or the titlebar panel toggle. 2. Run your package manager install command: Use pnpm install , yarn , or bun install if that is what the project expects. Wait for install to finish before starting the dev server.
chunks.title: First Project

chunks.heading: Start the dev server
chunks.text: Option A: click Scripts in the titlebar and choose dev (or start ). Option B: type in the terminal: The terminal shows the local URL (often http://localhost:3000 or similar). Open it in your browser to confirm the app runs.
chunks.title: First Project

chunks.heading: Edit a file
chunks.text: 1. Press Ctrl+P and type the name of a component or page file. 2. Make a visible change (for example edit a heading string). 3. Save with Ctrl+S . The browser should hot reload if the dev server supports it.
chunks.title: First Project

chunks.heading: Check for problems
chunks.text: Press Ctrl+Shift+M to open the Problems panel. Fix any TypeScript or ESLint issues the project reports.
chunks.title: First Project

chunks.text: 1. Open AI Chat from the titlebar. 2. Select Ask mode. 3. Ask: "What does the main entry file do?" Review the answer without applying edits. Sign in with a Shape account if prompted.

chunks.text: This tutorial shows a safe AI assisted refactor: extract a repeated utility, update call sites, and review every diff before accepting.
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.heading: Prepare
chunks.text: 1. Open a project folder in Shape. 2. Sign in to your Shape account for AI access. 3. Open AI Chat from the titlebar. Pick a small, well scoped task, such as "Move duplicated date formatting into lib/format date.ts and update imports."
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.heading: Optional: Plan first
chunks.text: For larger refactors, start in Plan mode: 1. Select Plan from the mode dropdown. 2. Describe the refactor and which files you think are involved. 3. Send the message. The assistant researches the codebase and saves a plan to .shape/plans/ . Open that file in the editor, edit if needed, then continue in Code mode.
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.heading: Run in Code mode
chunks.text: 1. Switch the dropdown to Code . 2. Send a clear instruction, for example: Create lib/format date.ts with a formatDate function. Replace inline toLocaleDateString calls in components/ with imports from the new module. Do not change unrelated files. 3. Wait for the assistant to propose edits.
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.heading: Review each edit
chunks.text: Each changed file appears as a card in the chat thread. 1. Click Preview to open a diff tab. 2. Read added and removed lines. 3. Click Accept only when the change looks correct. 4. Click Reject on anything that touches files outside scope. Do not enable auto apply until you are comfortable with the workflow. See Reviewing Edits.
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.heading: Verify
chunks.text: After accepting edits: 1. Save all files ( Ctrl+K S ). 2. Open Problems ( Ctrl+Shift+M ) and fix new type errors. 3. Run tests or the dev server from the terminal: If the assistant proposed a terminal command, approve Run on the card and check output in the panel.
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.heading: Iterate
chunks.text: If something failed, send a follow up in the same thread: The test in format date.test.ts fails because of timezone. Fix the test to use UTC. Review and accept the follow up edits the same way.
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.heading: What you learned
chunks.text: Use Plan for design and Code for implementation Preview and accept edits one file at a time Verify with Problems and terminal commands
chunks.title: Refactor with AI

chunks.text: This tutorial covers cloning a repository, committing a change, and pushing to GitHub using Shape's Git UI.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: From the welcome screen
chunks.text: 1. Click Clone Repository . 2. Paste a Git URL, for example https://github.com/org/repo.git . 3. Choose a parent folder on disk. Shape runs git clone in the terminal.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: Open the clone
chunks.text: After cloning, open the new folder with File → Open Folder and select the repository directory.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: Sign in to GitHub
chunks.text: For HTTPS remotes, sign in with GitHub from the avatar menu before pushing. This avoids repeated credential prompts. Your Shape account (for AI) and GitHub sign in are separate. See Accounts.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: Make a change
chunks.text: 1. Open a file from the Explorer. 2. Edit and save ( Ctrl+S ). 3. Open Source Control ( Ctrl+Shift+G ). The file appears under Changes . Click it to open a diff tab and review what changed.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: Commit
chunks.text: 1. Click + next to the file to stage it (or stage all from the Changes header). 2. Enter a commit message, for example docs: fix typo in readme . 3. Click Commit . Optional: click the sparkle icon for an AI suggested commit message from your diff.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: Push
chunks.text: 1. Check the current branch in the Source Control header. 2. Click Push (up arrow) in the toolbar. 3. If prompted, complete GitHub authentication. Use Sync to pull remote changes first when the status bar shows you are behind the remote.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: View history
chunks.text: Open Git Graph from the activity bar to see your commit in the lane diagram. Right click it to inspect files or compare with the working tree.
chunks.title: Clone and Commit

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting push
chunks.text: Issue Fix Authentication failed Sign out and sign in again from the avatar GitHub menu Rejected non fast forward Click Pull , resolve conflicts if any, then push No remote configured Add origin in the remotes dialog. See Branches and Remotes

chunks.heading: What it means
chunks.text: Your account session expired, was revoked, or you signed out elsewhere.
chunks.title: 1002 Session expired

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Sign in again from the app or login. 2. If you changed your password or enabled 2FA, complete the new challenge. 3. If it keeps happening, revoke sessions in the dashboard and sign in once.

chunks.heading: What it means
chunks.text: Sign in did not finish. The browser flow may have failed, timed out, or returned an error.

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Try Sign in again from the app. 2. Complete login in the browser window that opens, then return to Shape. 3. Check that you can reach useshape.org and that you have an invite if signup is required. 4. If it keeps failing, sign in on the dashboard first, then retry from the app.

chunks.heading: What it means
chunks.text: The editor, agent, or a tool could not access a file or folder. Common causes: missing permissions, a deleted file, or a path outside the open workspace.
chunks.title: 4000 Workspace or file access

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Confirm the folder still exists and you can edit it. 2. Re open the project in Shape. 3. On Windows, check whether antivirus is locking files. 4. If an agent used a path outside the workspace, reject it and ask again with an in project path.
chunks.title: 4000 Workspace or file access

chunks.heading: What it means
chunks.text: Shape could not complete a Git action (status, commit, push, pull, branch, or fetch). Common causes: bad credentials, no remote, a locked .git/index.lock , or merge conflicts.
chunks.title: 4100 Git failed

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Confirm the folder is a Git repo and you have a remote if you are pushing. 2. If you see a lock error, close other Git tools and delete a stale .git/index.lock only when no Git process is running. 3. Sign in to GitHub from Shape if the remote needs auth. 4. Resolve merge conflicts, then retry.
chunks.title: 4100 Git failed

chunks.text: Source control GitHub sign in Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: What it means
chunks.text: IntelliSense, go to definition, or diagnostics stopped because a language server exited or never started. Editing still works; language features may be limited.
chunks.title: 4200 Language server

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Re open the file or the project folder. 2. Check Settings → Languages and confirm the server for this file type is enabled. 3. For TypeScript/JavaScript, ensure node modules (or your toolchain) is installed. 4. Watch Output → LSP for the underlying message, then retry.
chunks.title: 4200 Language server

chunks.heading: What it means
chunks.text: File search, content search, or AI codebase indexing could not run. Causes include a missing search binary, a corrupt index, or a folder Shape cannot read.
chunks.title: 4300 Index or search

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Confirm the project folder is still open and readable. 2. Retry search, or re run indexing from Settings → AI . 3. On Windows, check antivirus exclusions for the project and Shape install. 4. If content search mentions ripgrep, reinstall Shape or ensure the bundled search tool is present.
chunks.title: 4300 Index or search

chunks.heading: What it means
chunks.text: Shape could not open a terminal session or run a shell command. Often the configured shell path is wrong, missing, or blocked by policy.
chunks.title: 4400 Terminal

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Open Settings and confirm your default shell path. 2. Try launching the same shell outside Shape. 3. On Windows, prefer a full path to powershell.exe or cmd.exe if PATH is incomplete. 4. Re open the terminal tab after fixing the shell.
chunks.title: 4400 Terminal

chunks.heading: What to do
chunks.text: 1. Try Help → Check for Updates again. 2. Confirm you are online and can reach Shape’s update servers. 3. If install keeps failing, download the latest installer from download and run it manually.

chunks.text: Error 1001: Offline Shape could not reach its servers. This is usually a network problem or a temporary service interruption.
chunks.title: Offline

chunks.heading: What to try
chunks.text: 1. Check that you are online and that firewalls or VPNs are not blocking Shape. 2. Wait a moment and try again if the service may be temporarily unavailable. 3. Confirm the Shape website loads in your browser. Local editing still works offline. Account sync and AI features need a connection.

chunks.heading: What to try
chunks.text: 1. Retry the request after a short wait. 2. Switch to a different model and try again. 3. Check status and billing if failures continue across models.

chunks.heading: What to try
chunks.text: 1. Check your plan and remaining credits on the billing page. 2. Use Auto if you are on the free tier, or wait for monthly Auto allowance to reset. 3. Upgrade your plan if you need more premium model capacity.

chunks.title: Network timeout

chunks.heading: What to try
chunks.text: 1. Check your connection and retry. 2. Disable or adjust VPN / proxy settings if requests fail only from this network. 3. Try again later if the path to Shape or the model provider is unstable.

chunks.title: Official build required

chunks.heading: What to try
chunks.text: 1. Install Shape from download. 2. Open the official app (not a custom or fork build) and sign in again.
